In 1807, Napoleon was defeated. By rabbits.
He had just signed a peace treaty, and wanted to celebrate with a rabbit hunt.
So his chief of staff, Louis-Alexandre Berthier, had hundreds of rabbits gathered for the day. Some accounts say up to three thousand.
The hunters lined up. The cages opened.
But the rabbits didn't run away. They ran straight at Napoleon.
Hundreds of them swarmed his legs, and started climbing up his coat.
His men tried to chase them off with whips and sticks.
Nothing worked. The emperor of France retreated to his carriage.
Even then, the rabbits split into two groups, surrounded the carriage, and some jumped inside.
Why? Berthier had bought tame rabbits from farmers. They thought Napoleon was bringing their dinner.
The man who conquered half of Europe, chased off the field by bunnies. At least, according to one of his generals.
